title: Distributed Induced Path Detection via Local Counting in a Height-Balanced Search Structure
topic: A Local-Counting Approach for Distributed Induced Path Detection
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight, locality-aware method for detecting induced paths in distributed graphs by leveraging a local counting mechanism atop a height-balanced search tree. The algorithm maintains a per-node counter that aggregates path participation counts during distributed traversal, enabling each node to decide locally whether it lies on an induced path of a specified length. We prove that the tree remains strictly height-balanced, guaranteeing $O(\log N)$ point and range queries as well as $O(\log N)$ insertion and rebalancing, where $N$ is the number of nodes. The implementation in C\# follows a purely functional style to avoid shared mutable state, and the source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/csharp-enterprise-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261127_190246_a_local-counting_approach_for}.
